note: Skeptic / future-maintainer angle. Changelog is noise (“Applied a search/replace patch” × N) — not scored as a plan defect. Findings below are against the draft as a Foreman-ready, long-lived build contract.

findings.section: Schedule, critical path; Waves 8–13 Depends on
findings.criterion: 3 (commission confirm + who), 6 (two skills), 10 (one writer), Wave-0 kill gate; and the plan’s own claim that `Depends on:` is the machine-checkable DAG
findings.message: The plan asserts `Depends on:` is the machine-checkable DAG, then systematically under-specifies it. Wave 10 only depends on Wave 9, yet its done-when requires G4 PASS (Wave 4), table-bound skill selection from `commissionable-skills.json` (Waves 4+5), and pid into the dossier (Wave 7). Wave 9 only depends on Wave 8, yet MUST import Wave 5’s calibration and justify envelope defaults against p90. Wave 13 only depends on Wave 12, yet multi-skill proof and handback validation require executor evidence, halt_class, and dossier. Lane D is said to join at 5→9/10/17 — not at Wave 8 — so a multi-lane run can batch-confirm scaffolding and record `who` (Wave 8) before G6 identity is locked (Wave 5). A future maintainer (and Foreman) will either invent missing edges or ship waves against missing substrates. Refute: either the DAG is complete and enforced, or “machine-checkable” is false advertising. Expand every Depends-on to every artifact actually imported; make lane joins equal Depends-on edges, including Wave 8 → Wave 5 if `who` is real.

findings.criterion: 12 (altitude within one poll; zero ambient when idle); 13 (index has stage/runs/attention without root walk)
findings.message: The seam table carefully splits pure `deriveAttention` from `publishAttention`, and Wave 15 names emitters for needs_you / deliverable_ready / blocked. It never names the mandatory call sites, the invoker, or the ordering relative to the state transition that creates the edge. Who calls `publishAttention` after commission-proposed, after handback, after kill, after queue? Session tick? Spine post-commit hook? High Seat poll (forbidden if it writes)? If nothing is obligated to call publish on those edges, a pure function and an idempotent publisher can both be green while the badge stays wrong forever — exactly the “plumbing green, outcomes red” failure criterion 9 forbids. Future maintainers will wire one path and miss others; flapping and stale packets reappear as integration folklore. Refute: name every transition → publish call site as a deliverable with a test that fails if the call is removed, and state that High Seat never publishes.

findings.criterion: 3 (confirm records who / bind is real); 8 (status = actual session state); 10 (exactly one roadmap_events writer); 11 (continuity after kill mid-flight)
findings.message: A4 is fixed by “one journaled transaction (or a crash-repairable pair with a named repair path)” across writeProjectRoadmap and Strip. That is two mechanisms with different failure modes, and neither is specified enough to implement without invention. What is the journal? Is Strip inside the typed-store allow-list and the single spine, or a second durable store with its own lock? If “repair path,” what is the detector, the repair verb, the idempotence key, and the user-visible state while unrepaired? Kill-between-writes is promised, but a future maintainer cannot choose between true multi-store atomicity and repair-after-crash from this text — and criterion 11’s dead-run / missing-handback naming depends on never leaving an orphaned bind that looks “confirmed.” Refute: pick ONE mechanism; name the stores in the transaction; name the repair algorithm and its tests; forbid “or” as a done-when.

findings.criterion: 6 (two different commissioned skills, test-bound); gate Decision 6
findings.message: Wave 4 writes `executor_proven` / evidence; Wave 5 writes `halt_class` / `excluded_reason`; a checked-in function derives `commissionable`. There is no merge protocol, lock, ordering, or schema version for that file. Lanes C and D are both off the critical path and can finish in either order; concurrent or out-of-order writes can clobber columns, leave half-rows, or recompute `commissionable` from stale peers. The plan’s whole answer to “never hand-pick skills” is this file — a second informal ledger with two writers, the exact risk taxonomy class it claims to kill for `roadmap_events`. Future maintainers will patch JSON by hand “just this once.” Refute: one writer API for the file, column-level update semantics, and a concurrency/repeat test; or regenerate the whole file from two pure inputs in a single wave join.

findings.topic: storage backend fork on hammer fail
findings.criterion: 10 (one writer + concurrency proof); durability obligations mapped to Waves 1 and 6
findings.message: If the target-box file hammer fails, Wave 1 “escalates to SQLite WAL, never a hardened file.” That is not a test failure — it is an unplanned architecture branch that rewrites the spine Wave 6 is supposed to own, without a decision record, schema, migration, or second-path test matrix. A future maintainer inherits either a silent SQLite production path or a plan that claimed file atomic-write+lock while the box runs WAL. Criterion 10’s concurrency test and the removal-proof durability gate become path-dependent. Refute: FAIL the wave and HALT for a storage decision; do not authorize a backend swap inside a ground-truth wave.

findings.criterion: 12 (typed projection = working | needs_you | deliverable_ready | blocked | idle)
findings.message: Criterion 12’s altitude contract is a closed five-state set. Wave 15 adds `unknown` as a named projection state when the store is unreadable (honesty-good) without amending the North Star or defining whether High Seat treat unknown as blocked, as a non-raise, or as a fourth ambient class. Future maintainers will disagree in fold/badge code; tests will pin whichever fork shipped first. Refute: either amend the locked contract to include `unknown` (or a structured failure envelope beside the five states), or map unreadable → a specified existing state plus a separate failure flag the fold understands — in one place both Wave 15 and 16 import.

findings.section: Attention publish seam; Wave 3 A5; Wave 15 index delivery
findings.criterion: 13 (consume EXISTING portfolio index, no root walk); Non-goal 1 (do not re-plan/rebuild portfolio tracking)
findings.message: Delivery “via existing anchor-contract ingest” for a new `attention` cell is asserted as wire-not-rebuild. If the live index does not already carry that cell (A5 may mark NEEDS-WIRE), wiring is either a schema extension of steward-tracking’s contract or a side-channel the no-walk query does not know. The plan never names the frozen index schema version, which fields are already present, or what NEEDS-WIRE is allowed to change without violating the non-goal. Future maintainers will “just add a column” and call it consume. Refute: Wave 3 must emit a hard ANSWERED vs NEEDS-WIRE vs REQUIRES-INDEX-CONTRACT-CHANGE trichotomy; the third is an explicit John HALT, not a Wave 15 fix item.

findings.criterion: 3 (skill + seat + depth before spend); Risk taxonomy (seat family/driver collision)
findings.message: Proposals that “name a colliding seat” are refused with a named error, but collision is never defined: same family? same driver process? same live job_id? same machine GPU? live lease only or also parked? Without a predicate and a source of truth for “occupied seats,” the guard is unimplementable and untestable; future maintainers will hard-code one product’s seating law and break another. Refute: one pure function `seatCollision(proposal, liveRuns) → ok|collision-reason` with fixtures, owned by a named wave, imported by Wave 10.

findings.criterion: 4 (REFLECTION RECEIPT with Oranges prompts); 1 (Oranges on scaffolding)
findings.message: The receipt is ALWAYS EMITTED as deterministic, zero-model, zero-spend from the dossier — while criterion 4 still requires Oranges prompts on that receipt. The plan never specifies which dossier fields supply those prompts (scaffold annotations? handback fields? empty templates?), the receipt schema, or the golden fixture that pins content. Future maintainers will either reintroduce a model call “to write Oranges” (breaking the envelope split) or emit empty Oranges and claim criterion 4. Refute: freeze a receipt schema with explicit Oranges field provenance (ledger-only), golden bytes, and a test that fails if a model is invoked on the emit path.

findings.section: Wave 5 compile-cost measurement; Wave 9 envelope bounds
findings.message: Wave 5 requires ≥20 real compiles (median/p90 $ and wall clock) while depending only on Wave 1 — before dialogue→step_create (Wave 8) and before the envelope that meters compiles (Wave 9). What is being compiled, on what path, under what auth, and is that spend inside a temporary envelope or outside the product law? Defaults ($5 / 25 / 240) “justified against p90” become either fictional or produced by an off-contract spend harness a future maintainer cannot replay. Refute: define the calibration harness as fixture compiles with recorded costs, or move calibration after the real compile path exists and make Wave 9 depend on that artifact explicitly (see Finding 1).

findings.criterion: 7 (stage artifacts render reviewably; correction → new version)
findings.message: G2 FAIL “routes a plan-shaped renderer into the chamber-UI wave.” Wave 17’s deliverable set is therefore contingent on a spike verdict, not frozen at plan approval. Foreman and future maintainers cannot cost, test-plan, or refuse scope creep against a moving chamber. Criterion 7 either always needs a plan-shaped renderer (put it in Wave 17 unconditionally) or G2 FAIL is a HALT/scope decision, not a silent deliverable injection. Refute: freeze Wave 17’s artifact renderer obligations in the plan text; spikes may only PASS or HALT with a named addendum, not mutate later waves.

findings.section: Wave 6 — CI invariant check / static check
findings.message: “Direct-write attempts fail a static/CI check” is asserted without naming the enforcement mechanism (AST allow-list of callables? package export only? runtime proxy?). Concurrency tests prove the happy path through the spine; they do not prove a future module cannot `fs.writeFile` the events file. Future maintainers will add a “temporary” bypass that CI never saw. Refute: name the check (e.g. only the spine module may import the events path; grep/AST gate on path string + write APIs) and a deliberate-violation test that fails the build when a second call site is introduced — same standard as the trio/index diff fence in Wave 1.

findings.criterion: Wave-0 kill gate timing; criteria 5, 8, 4 as independently shippable proofs
findings.message: Progressive elaboration (11), session-state truth (12), and handback/reflection (13) are chained as if each required the previous. Nothing in the North Star says status-across-kill depends on stage-start questions, or that multi-skill handback depends on progressive elaboration. The false chain hides real parallelism and teaches future maintainers the wrong dependency graph (compounding Finding 1). Refute: Depends-on only true artifact edges; keep narrative “recommended order” separate from the DAG.

findings.section: Wave 6 APPEND IDEMPOTENCE; Waves 8–10, 13, 15 double-submit tests
findings.criterion: 2/3 (confirm once); risk of double spend; idempotence gates
findings.message: Every idempotent confirm hangs on caller-supplied `client_event_id`, but no owner mints it, no uniqueness scope (session vs project vs global), and no collision behavior is defined. Future UI authors will reuse button handlers or omit ids and get silent no-ops or double commits. Refute: specify mint site (client ULID per user intent), persistence until ack, and server behavior on malformed/missing ids.

findings.criterion: 3 (skill + seat + depth before spend; nothing spent unconfirmed)
findings.message: Proposals must show estimated spend before confirmation, but no estimator, units, or honest-unknown path is specified. Maintainers will hard-code “$0” or omit the field and still paint the proposal green. Refute: named estimate function or explicit `estimate: unknown` with UI copy; test that confirmation still requires who when estimate is unknown.

findings.section: Document header NS paste + Success criteria restatement
findings.criterion: Anti-drift authority (all elements serve locked NS)
findings.message: The full North Star is inlined, then success criteria are restated with gate decisions layered in. Future edits will drift the two. Maintainers will not know which text is normative. Refute: one normative pointer to NORTH-STAR.md plus a criteria checklist that does not re-author the statement; gate decisions live in a single DECISIONS section.

findings.criterion: 9 (auth ON, outcomes); Wave-0 kill gate as a runnable suite
findings.message: `test-command: node scripts/run-all-tests.mjs` is declared with no wave that creates the runner, wires auth-ON-only, or maps property-gate checkboxes to named tests. Checkbox lists stay forever unchecked theater. Refute: a substrate wave deliverable for the runner + a machine-readable map gate-id → test-id updated as waves land.

DEGRADED appears as one-run-at-a-time executor, A5 field cap overflow, G4 anchor-fallback, and W18 gate report — no single checked-in `artifacts/degraded.json` future operators can read without mining four waves. Not a loop-stopper if W18 lists them, but maintainers will miss mid-run degrade. Prefer one append-only degraded ledger from the first wave that can emit one.
